metadata.name: Resident Households
metadata.definition: Annual number of resident households; household counts are distinct from population and are not the number of newly formed households.
metadata.update_frequency: Annual observation frequency in official metadata; expected update cadence is inferred, not guaranteed. Individual observation publication dates are not confirmed.
metadata.table_title: Resident Households By Household Size, Annual
metadata.source_footnote: Data for 1980, 1990, 2000, 2010 and 2020 are based on the Census of Population while data for 1995, 2005, 2015 and 2025 are based on the General Household Survey. Data for all other years are based on the Comprehensive June Labour Force Survey. Survey estimates are subject to sampling variability.
metadata.scope: Resident households. Source estimates combine Census of Population, General Household Survey and Comprehensive June Labour Force Survey; sampling variability and source changes apply.

mechanism.sales: Household counts may better represent potential dwelling demand than population alone, subject to tenure, household composition and affordability.
mechanism.rents: More households may support rental demand depending on tenure choices.
mechanism.lag: Annual structural context; no short-term timing claim.
mechanism.limitations: Differences in household counts are not gross household formation. Census and survey years use different sources; metadata does not establish one exact reference day for every year. Period-end filtering is conservative and is not a claim that the count was measured at year-end.

metadata.name: Median Monthly Household Employment Income Including Employer CPF Contributions
metadata.definition: Median nominal monthly household employment income among resident employed households, including employer CPF contributions and one-twelfth of annual bonus, before Government transfers and taxes.
metadata.update_frequency: Annual observation frequency in official metadata; expected update cadence is inferred, not guaranteed. Individual observation publication dates are not confirmed.
metadata.table_title: Key Indicators On Household Employment Income Among Resident Employed Households, Annual
metadata.source_footnote: Data refer to resident employed households. A resident employed household refers to a household where the household reference person is a resident (i.e. Singapore citizen or permanent resident), and with at least one employed person. Household employment income refers to the sum of income received by employed members of the household from employment and business, excluding the income of live-in domestic workers. Monthly household employment income includes employer Central Provident Fund (CPF) contributions and one-twelfth of annual bonus. Data on household employment income refers to household employment income before accounting for Government transfers and taxes, unless stated otherwise.
metadata.scope: Households whose reference person is a citizen or permanent resident and with at least one employed member. Income sums employment and business income of employed household members, excluding live-in domestic workers.

mechanism.sales: Median household employment income may describe typical household purchasing capacity more directly than mean income per employed person.
mechanism.rents: Median household income may contextualise household rent affordability.
mechanism.lag: Annual affordability context; income and financing decisions can adjust over subsequent quarters.
mechanism.limitations: Not income per household member or an individual wage. Excludes households with no employed person; includes employer CPF and annual bonus allocation, unlike the existing bonus-excluding quarterly individual mean. Nominal and not take-home income.

metadata.name: Employment (Persons) As At Year End
metadata.definition: Total persons in employment as at year-end, expressed in thousands; includes migrant domestic workers and excludes persons serving two-year full-time national service.
metadata.update_frequency: Annual observation frequency in official metadata; expected update cadence is inferred, not guaranteed. Individual observation publication dates are not confirmed.
metadata.row_footnote: Data are compiled primarily from administrative records, wtih the self-employed component estimated from the Labour Force Survey.
metadata.scope: Resident and non-resident employees plus self-employed persons. MOM administrative-record coverage excludes two-year full-time national servicemen; the current MOM summary identifies the matching total as including migrant domestic workers. SingStat row footnote confirms administrative records plus Labour Force Survey estimates for the self-employed.

mechanism.sales: A larger employment base may support aggregate earned income and housing purchasing capacity.
mechanism.rents: Employment expansion may support work-related housing and rental demand.
mechanism.lag: Annual year-end employment context; housing responses need not be simultaneous.
mechanism.limitations: Counts employed persons, not vacancies, new hires or the unemployment rate. Includes migrant domestic workers and other workers whose accommodation need is not an ordinary separate rental unit. Employment and housing may share common causes; not a residents-only series.

metadata.name: Total HDB Flats
metadata.definition: Total HDB flats as at end-June of each year, including non-privatised Housing and Urban Development Corporation flats.
metadata.update_frequency: Annual observation frequency in official metadata; expected update cadence is inferred, not guaranteed. Individual observation publication dates are not confirmed.
metadata.source_footnote: Data as at end June of each year.
metadata.row_footnote: Includes non-privatised Housing and Urban Development Corporation flats.
metadata.scope: Public-housing dwelling stock; not annual completions, BTO launches, resale transactions or flats available for rent.

mechanism.sales: The public-housing stock adds supply context not represented by private residential stock and may influence tenure and purchase choices.
mechanism.rents: Public-housing supply can affect tenure choices and rental alternatives subject to eligibility and rental rules.
mechanism.lag: Annual supply stock; allocations, completion and occupation timing can differ.
mechanism.limitations: Stock is not new supply or vacancies and includes non-privatised HUDC flats. Public and private markets differ in eligibility and policy; aggregate stock alone does not predict prices or rents.

metadata.name: Median Monthly Household Market Income
metadata.definition: Median nominal monthly household market income among resident households, before Government transfers and taxes.
metadata.update_frequency: Annual observation frequency in official metadata; expected update cadence is inferred, not guaranteed. Individual observation publication dates are not confirmed.
metadata.table_title: Key Indicators On Household Market Income Among Resident Households, Annual
metadata.source_footnote: Data refer to resident households.  A resident household refers to a household where the household reference person is a resident (i.e. Singapore citizen or permanent resident).  Household market income refers to income received by households from the market economy before any Government transfers and taxes.  It comprises income from employment (including one-twelfth of annual bonuses and employer CPF contributions) and non-employment sources including investments (such as interests from savings and/or CPF balances, dividends from investments), rental, contributions from other households (such as allowance from children to parents not staying in the same household, alimony), pensions, annuities, royalties and regular payouts from CPF and insurance (i.e. CPF ElderShield and CareShield Life).  This income concept aligns with international standards, which define income as regular monetary or in-kind receipts available for current consumption without diminishing net worth.  The dollar values are in nominal terms.  Data for the latest year are preliminary. More data and analyses on household income can be found in the paper 'Key Household Income Trends, 2025'.  The paper can be accessed via the following web-link: https://www.singstat.gov.sg/find-data/explore-data-themes/households/household-income/related-information.
metadata.scope: Employment income including employer CPF and one-twelfth of annual bonus plus investment, rental, inter-household contributions, pension and other regular market income; includes resident households without employed members.

mechanism.sales: Broader household resources may contextualise housing purchasing capacity.
mechanism.rents: Broader household resources may contextualise rent affordability.
mechanism.limitations: Overlaps the employment-income candidate; includes rental income, which can respond to the housing outcome. Latest year preliminary. Not employment income or per-member income.

metadata.name: Total Changes In Employment
metadata.definition: Net change in persons employed at quarter-end compared with the preceding quarter-end.
metadata.update_frequency: Quarterly observation frequency in official metadata; expected update cadence is inferred, not guaranteed. Individual observation publication dates are not confirmed.
metadata.table_title: Changes In Employment By Sector, (Compared To The Previous Period), Quarterly
metadata.source_footnote: Employment change refers to the change in the number of persons who are in employment, derived by taking the difference in the employment level at the end of the reference period compared with the end of the preceding period.  A positive change refers to the additional number of persons who are in employment, while a negative change refers to the decline in number of persons in employment.  Data may not add up to the total due to rounding.  The industries are classified based on SSIC 2020 from 2009 onwards and SSIC 2005 from 2002 to 2008.  Data are revised at the industry level to reflect updates in industry classification of firms based on SSIC 2020.
metadata.scope: Total change in employment across sectors, in persons; positive and negative values are net additions and losses.

mechanism.sales: Employment gains may support aggregate earning capacity and housing demand.
mechanism.rents: Employment gains may support work-related rental demand.
mechanism.lag: Quarterly labour activity; housing responses may lag.
mechanism.limitations: Already a first difference, not employment level. Further changes measure a change in net job additions. Non-seasonally adjusted; use same-quarter comparisons. Classification changes affect industry detail.
